A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiBanana study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained experiments and supplementary material can be matched despite substantial reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five image-generation models, reference-count and difficulty analyses, and experiments with three agentic frameworks.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original human–VLM agreement, judge consistency, synthetic-reference bias, and prompt-priority results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline and IPR, CAFG, and SRA algorithms retain their procedures, equations, planner/generator pairings, and prompts. The additional Qwen3-VL judge extends evaluation rather than changing the generation algorithms.

E1.justification: The core benchmark, languages, reference counts, and external benchmark coverage are retained. Appendix F.5 adds cross-domain scenarios explicitly prioritizing reference consistency or background–subject matching. The 48-to-24 multi-reference task-count revision does not establish removal of evaluated coverage: both versions report the same 24-task grid.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct as an evaluated alternative to GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 in the judge comparison against human ratings (Table 4). The image-generation comparator set and the IPR, CAFG, and SRA comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include three human evaluators rating 32 samples, Qwen3-VL-only benchmark scoring, partitioning by synthetic-reference source, and priority-instruction tests on 20 prompts. The new Qwen-judged results explicitly use January 2026 versions of the closed generators. The original five scoring criteria and their weights remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands benchmark validation through direct human agreement, judge self-consistency, synthetic-source bias analysis, and tests of competing cross-domain criteria (Section 4.4 and Appendices E and F.4–F.5). Existing reference-count, difficulty, model-sensitivity, and agent-step analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 already reports cross-VLM correlations with 95% confidence intervals over ten subsets. v2 additionally reports standard errors across three random seeds, 99% confidence intervals for reference-source comparisons, and Pearson, Spearman, and Cohen’s kappa statistics against human ratings. These are new reporting practices, not an established increase in runs for the original experiments.

E6.justification: Original benchmark tables and matched plots retain their numerical results. v2 adds extensive Qwen-judged scores, human agreement coefficients, seed errors, source-bias results, and prompt-priority outcomes. It also changes the background-task weakness attribution from Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 to Nano Banana. The new Qwen-judged scores involve different judge and generator settings and therefore do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The agentic-framework equations and scoring weights are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs; the added validation statistics and conceptual discussion do not change the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: Both versions present MultiBanana as a challenging benchmark covering up to eight references and heterogeneous reference conditions. The central findings about omitted subjects versus compositional distortion remain. v2 foregrounds findings already present in v1 and adds supporting validation without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of synthetic-source favoritism, compatibility between reference fidelity and scene coherence, and practical advertising applications. Appendix I newly identifies the exclusion of temporal generation and ambiguity of natural-language spatial instructions. Appendix F.2 also revises and qualifies the explanation of Qwen’s failure threshold.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds a dataset-access link, exact judge API identifiers, and generator-version dates. Appendix E.4 reports evaluation costs of approximately $44 for GPT-5 and $29 for Gemini 2.5. Existing construction thresholds, agent settings, and complete evaluation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens research positioning through comparisons with MultiRef-Bench, RealEdit, and SpotEdit, plus a dedicated discussion connecting multi-reference generation to LLM instruction following. Additional literature supports applications, video-conditioning limitations, and structured-layout alternatives; these works are not newly evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The introduction, task rationale, and supplementary prose undergo extensive editing and condensation. Duplicative extended related work is rewritten, the reliability discussion is reorganized, and appendix ordering and prompt documentation are consolidated. Task-count and category-count inconsistencies are also corrected.

P2.justification: v2 adds displays for human agreement, Qwen-judged results, seed consistency, synthetic-source bias, and prompt priorities, alongside new qualitative examples. Retained quantitative and qualitative figures are extensively regrouped, the IPR example is relocated, and Figures 6 and 7 exchange order. Example prompt labels and the construction diagram are also revised.

improvement.justification: v1 relied on proprietary judges supported mainly by prior work and inter-judge agreement. v2 substantially strengthens this central benchmark dependency through direct human validation, an open-weight evaluation option, consistency checks, and bias analyses, supported by clearer reproducibility information and limitations. The human study remains small, and Table 15 shows declines in unprioritized scores despite claims of maintaining them, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and accessibility.
